title: Glossy Salmon Teriyaki
summary: Pan-seared salmon fillets with crisp skin, finished in a sticky honey-soy glaze that comes together in the same pan.
equipment: large non-stick or well-seasoned frying pan (28-30 cm)

steps.title: Mix the Sauce
steps.text: Whisk the soy sauce, honey, water, rice vinegar, ginger and garlic together in a bowl, then stir the cornflour and cold water in a separate small bowl until smooth. Keeping the cornflour apart and fully dispersed in cold liquid first stops it clumping when it later hits the hot pan. Both mixtures can sit ready while you prepare the fish.

steps.title: Dry and Season Fish
steps.text: Take the salmon out of the fridge 10 minutes before cooking so it cooks more evenly, then pat the skin thoroughly dry with paper towel and season the flesh side lightly with salt. Dry skin is the key to a crisp result — any surface moisture turns to steam and makes the skin spit and stick rather than crisp. Leave the fillets skin-side up while the pan heats.

steps.title: Sear Skin Side
steps.text: Heat the oil in a 28-30 cm non-stick pan over medium-high until it shimmers, then lay the fillets in skin-side down, placing them away from you to avoid splashes. Press each one gently with a fish slice for about 10 seconds so the skin can't curl away from the heat. Cook undisturbed for 4-5 minutes: the opaque colour creeps roughly two-thirds up the sides, and the skin releases easily when nudged, a sign the fat underneath has rendered and crisped.

steps.title: Flip and Sear Flesh
steps.text: Turn each fillet over and cook for a further 1 minute on the flesh side. This brief sear sets the surface without overcooking the delicate flesh, leaving the centre ready to finish gently in the glaze.

steps.title: Build the Glaze
steps.text: Reduce the heat to medium-low, since honey scorches fast over high heat, then pour in the sauce and let it bubble for 1 minute. Stir in the cornflour slurry and simmer for a further 1-2 minutes, spooning the sauce over the fish as it thickens, until it's glossy enough to coat the back of a spoon. The salmon is ready when the thickest part reaches 55-60°C, flaking under gentle pressure with a centre just turned opaque — it keeps cooking slightly once off the heat.

steps.title: Finish and Serve
steps.text: Spoon the remaining glaze over the fillets and scatter with the toasted sesame seeds and sliced spring onions. Serve straight from the pan alongside steamed rice and greens to soak up the extra sauce.

tips: Don't crowd a cold pan — if the oil isn't shimmering before the fish goes in, or the fillets are touching, the skin will stick rather than crisp.
Resist moving the fish while the skin crisps; it needs the full 4-5 minutes undisturbed to release cleanly.
If the sauce reduces too far and turns too thick, loosen it with a splash of water off the heat.
Cooking skinless fillets instead? Sear for 2-3 minutes per side rather than following the skin-side timing.
Run a finger along each fillet before cooking to check for stray pin bones.
storage: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days — enjoy cold flaked over a salad, or reheat gently covered in a low oven at 150°C (130°C fan) for about 10 minutes until just warm, as high heat will dry the fish out. The sauce alone can be made up to 3 days ahead and kept chilled.
